source_text:
Οὐκ ἄρα ἀπορριπτέον τὰ καὶ τοὺς πέλας ὠφελοῦντα χρήματα·
κτήματα γάρ ἐστι κτητὰ ὄντα καὶ χρήματα χρήσιμα ὄντα καὶ εἰς χρῆσιν ἀνθρώπων ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ παρεσκευασμένα, ἃ δὴ παράκειται καὶ ὑποβέβληται καθάπερ ὕλη τις καὶ ὄργανα πρὸς χρῆσιν ἀγαθὴν τοῖς εἰδόσι. τὸ ὄργανον, ἐὰν χρῇ τεχνικῶς, τεχνικόν ἐστιν, ἐὰν ὑστερῇς τῆς τέχνης, ἀπολαύει τῆς σῆς ἀμουσίας, ὂν ἀναίτιον. τοιοῦτον καὶ ὁ πλοῦτος ὄργανόν ἐστι. δύνασαι χρῆσθαι δικαίως αὐτῷ· πρὸς δικαιοσύνην καθυπηρετεῖ· ἀδίκως τις αὐτῷ χρῆται· πάλιν ὑπηρέτης ἀδικίας εὑρίσκεται· πέφυκε γὰρ ὑπηρετεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἄρχειν. οὐ χρὴ τοίνυν τὸ ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ μὴ ἔχον μήτε τὸ ἀγαθὸν μήτε τὸ κακόν. ἀναίτιον ὄν, αἰτιᾶσθαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ δυνάμενον καὶ καλῶς τούτοις χρῆσθαι καὶ κακῶς, ἀφ᾿ ὧν ἂν ἕληται, κατ᾿ αὐτὸ τοῦτο αἴτιον ὄν. τοῦτο δ᾿ ἐστὶ νοῦς ἀνθρώπου. καὶ κριτήριον ἐλεύθερον ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ καὶ τὸ αὐτεξούσιον τῆς μεταχειρίσεως τῶν δοθέντων· ὥστε μὴ τὰ κτήματά τις ἀφανιζέτω μᾶλλον ἢ τὰ πάθη τῆς ψυχῆς, τὰ μὴ συγχωροῦντα τὴν ἀμείνω χρῆσιν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων. ἵνα καλὸς καὶ ἀγαθὸς γενόμενος καὶ τούτοις τοῖς κτήμασι χρῆσθαι δυνηθῇ καλῶς. τὸ οὖν ἀποτάξασθαι πᾶσι τοῖς ὑπάρχουσι καὶ πωλῆσαι πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον ἐκδεκτέον ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν ψυχικῶν παθῶν διειρημένον.
thought_title: Wealth as an instrument, not a cause
orientation: Clement is explaining that money and possessions are not to be thrown away, because they are instruments given by God for good use, and the real thing to renounce is the passions of the soul.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the money that also benefits neighbors must not be thrown away; for possessions are things acquired, being acquirable, and money is things useful, being useful, and prepared by God for the use of humans, which indeed lie ready and have been placed underneath just like some material and instruments for good use by those who know. The instrument, if you use it skillfully, is skillful, but if you fall short of the skill, it enjoys the fruit of your lack of culture, being without blame. Such an instrument also is wealth. You are able to use it justly; it serves for righteousness; someone uses it unjustly; again it is found a servant of injustice; for it has been born to serve, not to rule. Therefore one must not blame what has from itself neither the good nor the bad, being without blame, but what is able both to use these things well and badly, according to whatever it chooses, being by this very thing a cause. And this is the mind of a human being, having also a free judgment in itself and the power of self-determination in the handling of the things given; so that let no one destroy the possessions rather than the passions of the soul, which do not permit the better use of one's goods, in order that, having become beautiful and good, he may be able also to use these possessions well. Therefore the renouncing of all one's goods and the selling of all one's possessions must be received in this way, as spoken with reference to the passions of the soul.

choices.why: The verb means to cast off or throw away; the negation is emphatic and matches Clement's argument that money is not to be discarded.
Clement uses the philosophical pair of matter and tools; 'material' keeps the technical sense of ὕλη as raw stuff for use.

choices.english: enjoys the fruit of your lack of culture
choices.why: ἀπολαύει means to enjoy the fruit or benefit of something; here it is ironic, and ἀμουσία is literally lack of the Muses' arts, i.e., lack of culture or skill.

choices.term: πέφυκε γὰρ ὑπηρετεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἄρχειν
choices.english: for it has been born to serve, not to rule
choices.why: πέφυκε means 'it is by nature' or 'it has been born'; the contrast between serving and ruling is central to Clement's point that wealth is subordinate to the user.
rejected: for it is its nature to serve, not to rule
for it naturally serves, not rules

choices.english: the mind of a human being
choices.why: νοῦς is the intellect or mind, the seat of judgment; Clement identifies this as the true cause of good or bad use.
ἀφανίζω means to make disappear or destroy; the imperative is third person, and Clement is urging the reader not to destroy possessions but passions.

pass_b_english: So money that also benefits our neighbors must not be thrown away. Possessions are called possessions because they can be possessed, and money is called money because it is useful, prepared by God for human use. These things lie at hand and are placed beneath us like some material and instruments for good use by those who know how. If you use an instrument skillfully, it is skillful; if you lack the skill, it enjoys the fruit of your lack of culture, though it is without blame. Wealth is an instrument of this kind. You can use it justly, and it serves righteousness. Someone uses it unjustly, and it is found to be a servant of injustice. For it has been born to serve, not to rule. We must not blame what has neither good nor evil in itself and is without blame, but rather what is able to use these things well or badly, depending on what it chooses, and is for that very reason the cause. That is the mind of a human being, which has within itself a free judgment and the power of self-determination in handling what has been given. So let no one destroy possessions rather than the passions of the soul, which do not permit the better use of what one has. Then, having become good and noble, he will be able to use these possessions well. The command to renounce all that one has and sell all that one has must therefore be understood in this way, as spoken about the passions of the soul.

problems.quote: So money that benefits our neighbors must not be thrown away.
problems.source_quote: τὰ καὶ τοὺς πέλας ὠφελοῦντα χρήματα
problems.why: Greek says money that benefits things/goods, not “our neighbors”. The phrase “our neighbors” is added.
problems.fix: So money that is useful must not be thrown away.
problems.ruling: τοὺς πέλας = 'those near/neighbors'; translator correctly renders it. No addition. Claim is wrong.

edits.old: So money that benefits our neighbors must not be thrown away.
edits.new: So money that also benefits our neighbors must not be thrown away.

fixed: The Greek phrase is 'τὰ καὶ τοὺς πέλας ὠφελοῦντα χρήματα' — 'the money that also benefits neighbors.' The English omitted 'also' (καὶ), which is a real omission. The suggested fix to remove 'our neighbors' entirely is wrong because τοὺς πέλας does mean 'neighbors.' The correct fix is to restore 'also' to match the source.

last_rejected.quote: enjoys the fruit of your lack of culture
last_rejected.why: Greek says the instrument suffers from the user's lack of skill (ἀμουσίας = lack of skill), not culture.
last_rejected.fix: suffers from your lack of skill
last_rejected.ruling: ἀμουσία spans lack of skill/education/culture; 'lack of culture' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: but rather what is able to use these things well or badly, depending on what it chooses, and is for that very reason the cause
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀναίτιον ὄν, αἰτιᾶσθαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ δυνάμενον ... κατ᾿ αὐτὸ τοῦτο αἴτιον ὄν
last_rejected.why: Greek directs blame to the one who uses wealth, not to the wealth itself; English reverses agency.
last_rejected.fix: but rather the one who uses them well or badly, according to his choice, who is the true cause
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly blames the mind (τὸ δυνάμενον...αἴτιον ὄν), not wealth; agency matches Greek source.
